about: The classification vocabulary of OSCR (decisions D6 and D7): the facets, their allowed values, one-line definitions and synthetic examples. `value` is what the code and the annotation file use; `name` is the label shown to people; `id` is the key of the `categories` table (docs/PLATFORM_PLAN.md, section 4). The rules live in oscr/classify.py; the annotation guide is docs/ANNOTATION.md.

on_topic.name: Neuroscience
on_topic.definition: Neuroscience means research on the nervous system (brain, spinal cord, nerves, retina: their cells, circuits, development and diseases), or research on the mind that uses neural measures (recordings, imaging, stimulation, lesions, neural tissue). Psychology or psychiatry with questionnaires and behavior only is not neuroscience; neither is a paper where 'neural' only means an artificial neural network.

values.name: yes
values.definition: The paper studies the nervous system, or studies the mind with neural measures.
examples: an fMRI study of working memory in healthy adults
dopaminergic neuron loss in a mouse model of Parkinson's disease
a trial of an antiseizure drug in focal epilepsy

values.name: no
values.definition: Anything else, including psychology or psychiatry without neural measures and machine learning outside neuroscience.
examples: a questionnaire survey of stress among university students
a convolutional neural network that grades colon biopsies
cortical bone screws in hip surgery

modality.name: Modality
modality.definition: The kind of data the paper itself collects or analyses (for a review: the kind of data it discusses). List every modality that is a real part of the work, not those only mentioned in the background.

values.name: EEG
values.definition: Scalp electroencephalography, including event-related potentials (ERP) and sleep EEG.

values.name: MEG
values.definition: Magnetoencephalography (SQUID or optically pumped magnetometers).
examples: MEG source imaging of auditory responses

values.name: fMRI
values.definition: Functional MRI (BOLD), task or resting state.

values.name: structural MRI / diffusion
values.definition: MRI other than BOLD fMRI: anatomical (T1, T2, FLAIR), diffusion (DTI, tractography), perfusion, spectroscopy, quantitative MRI, clinical MRI reading.
examples: DTI tractography of the arcuate fasciculus
MRI lesion load in multiple sclerosis

values.name: PET / SPECT
values.definition: Positron emission tomography or single-photon emission tomography, including amyloid, tau, FDG and dopamine transporter scans.
examples: amyloid PET in preclinical Alzheimer's disease

values.name: fNIRS
values.definition: Functional near-infrared spectroscopy and diffuse optical tomography.
examples: prefrontal fNIRS during a dual task

values.name: intracranial EEG (iEEG / ECoG / SEEG)
values.definition: Human intracranial recordings: electrocorticography (ECoG), stereo-EEG (SEEG), depth electrodes, including local field potentials from deep brain stimulation leads.
examples: subthalamic beta activity recorded from DBS leads

values.name: extracellular electrophysiology (units, LFP)
values.definition: Extracellular recordings of single units, multi-unit activity or local field potentials, mostly in animals or in vitro (tetrodes, silicon probes, Neuropixels, microelectrode arrays); human microelectrode single units count here too.
examples: Neuropixels recordings in mouse visual cortex
hippocampal place cells recorded with tetrodes
a microelectrode array of cultured neurons

values.name: intracellular / patch clamp
values.definition: Intracellular recordings: patch clamp (whole-cell, voltage or current clamp), sharp electrodes, two-electrode voltage clamp.
examples: voltage clamp of a channel expressed in oocytes

values.name: optical imaging (calcium, voltage, 2-photon)
values.definition: Optical imaging of neural activity: calcium or voltage imaging (one- or two-photon, widefield, miniscopes), fiber photometry, intrinsic signal imaging.
examples: two-photon calcium imaging in mouse visual cortex
light-sheet calcium imaging of the larval zebrafish brain

values.name: behavior only
values.definition: Behavioral, cognitive or psychological measures only (tasks, tests, psychophysics, eye tracking, questionnaires, rating scales), with no neural recording or imaging.
examples: a psychophysics study of visual crowding
water-maze and open-field tests after a drug in rats

values.name: computational modeling (no new data)
values.definition: Computational modeling without new data: theory, simulations, models fitted to published data.
examples: a spiking network model of working memory
a neural mass model of seizure onset
a normative theory of grid cells

values.name: genetics / omics
values.definition: Genetics and omics: sequencing, genotyping, GWAS, transcriptomics (bulk, single-cell, spatial), proteomics, metabolomics, epigenomics.
examples: single-nucleus RNA-seq of the human cortex
a genome-wide association study of migraine
a de novo variant found by exome sequencing

values.name: histology / microscopy
values.definition: Histology and microscopy of tissue or cells: staining, immunohistochemistry, immunofluorescence, confocal or electron microscopy, tissue clearing, neuropathology.

values.name: other
values.definition: Any other data: clinical records and outcomes, blood or CSF biomarkers, EMG and other physiology, brain stimulation outcomes (TMS, tDCS), CT, ultrasound, retinal imaging, molecular assays (western blot, ELISA, qPCR).

organism.name: Organism
organism.definition: The species studied: where the subjects, tissue, cells or data come from. For in vitro work, the species the cells come from (human iPSC-derived neurons are human).

values.name: human
values.definition: Humans: participants, patients, human tissue or human cells.

values.name: mouse
values.definition: Mice, including transgenic lines and mouse cells.

values.name: rat
values.definition: Rats and rat cells.

values.name: non-human primate
values.definition: Non-human primates: macaques, marmosets and other monkeys.
examples: single units in macaque prefrontal cortex

values.name: zebrafish
values.definition: Zebrafish (Danio rerio).

values.name: drosophila
values.definition: Drosophila (fruit flies).

values.name: C. elegans
values.definition: Caenorhabditis elegans.
examples: a C. elegans model of neurodegeneration

values.name: other
values.definition: Any other species: other mammals (cats, dogs, pigs, ferrets, bats...), birds, amphibians, other fish, other invertebrates, and cells from other species.

values.name: none (in silico)
values.definition: No organism: pure theory, simulation, or a method tested on synthetic data.
examples: a filtering method tested on simulated signals

population.name: Population
population.definition: The condition studied. 'healthy' when the study is about typical subjects only (healthy people, wild-type animals, healthy aging); otherwise the condition(s). Healthy controls in a patient study do not add 'healthy'. An animal model of a disease counts as that disease. Write '-' when there are no subjects at all (pure theory, a simulation, a method on synthetic data).

values.name: healthy
values.definition: Typical subjects only; no condition studied.

values.name: epilepsy
values.definition: Epilepsy and seizures, including animal seizure models and developmental and epileptic encephalopathies.
examples: a kainate model of temporal lobe epilepsy

values.name: Alzheimer's / dementia
values.definition: Alzheimer's disease and other dementias, mild cognitive impairment, amyloid and tau models.
examples: amyloid PET in mild cognitive impairment

values.name: Parkinson's
values.definition: Parkinson's disease, parkinsonism and its models (MPTP, 6-OHDA, alpha-synuclein).

values.name: stroke
values.definition: Stroke and cerebrovascular disease: ischemic stroke, intracerebral or subarachnoid hemorrhage, aneurysms, small vessel disease, animal ischemia models.
examples: middle cerebral artery occlusion in mice

values.name: schizophrenia / psychosis
values.definition: Schizophrenia and psychosis, including clinical high risk and first episode.

values.name: depression
values.definition: Depression: major depressive disorder, depressive symptoms, treatment-resistant depression, depression models.
examples: rumination and fMRI in major depression
a chronic stress model of depression in mice

values.name: bipolar
values.definition: Bipolar disorder.

values.name: autism
values.definition: Autism spectrum disorder and autism models.

values.name: ADHD
values.definition: Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder.

values.name: multiple sclerosis
values.definition: Multiple sclerosis and its models (EAE, cuprizone).

values.name: traumatic brain injury
values.definition: Traumatic brain injury and concussion, and their models.

values.name: pain
values.definition: Pain: acute and chronic pain, nociception, neuropathic pain, headache and migraine.

values.name: sleep disorders
values.definition: Sleep disorders: insomnia, sleep apnea, narcolepsy, REM sleep behavior disorder, restless legs, circadian rhythm disorders. Sleep in healthy people is 'healthy'.

values.name: other condition
values.definition: Any other condition: brain tumors, ALS, Huntington's disease, ataxias, dystonia, neuropathies, spinal cord injury, infections, anxiety, PTSD, OCD, addiction, neurodevelopmental syndromes, hearing or vision loss, conditions outside the nervous system.

subfield.name: Subfield
subfield.definition: The paper's main angle. Pick one; when two fit equally well, pick the one that best describes the main question and name the other in the notes.

values.name: cognitive
values.definition: Cognitive neuroscience: perception, attention, memory, language, emotion, decision-making, consciousness, social cognition, usually with task-based measures.
examples: EEG of predictive processing in speech

values.name: systems
values.definition: Systems neuroscience: circuits, networks and neural coding; how populations of neurons and brain areas produce behavior, often in animals.

values.name: clinical / translational
values.definition: Clinical and translational neuroscience: diagnosis, prognosis, treatment and biomarkers of a condition, in patients or in disease models aimed at therapy; case reports.
examples: a trial of DBS for depression
MRI predictors of outcome after stroke
a case report of autoimmune encephalitis

values.name: computational
values.definition: Computational neuroscience: theory and models of neural function (biophysical, network, normative, cognitive models).
examples: a normative model of grid cells
a neural mass model of EEG rhythms

values.name: developmental
values.definition: Developmental neuroscience: development of the nervous system and of brain function, from embryo to adolescence (neurogenesis, migration, maturation).
examples: cortical interneuron migration in the embryo

values.name: cellular / molecular
values.definition: Cellular and molecular neuroscience: cells, synapses, channels, receptors, genes, signaling pathways, glia.
examples: a signaling pathway in neuronal survival

values.name: methods / tools
values.definition: Methods and tools: new methods, software, hardware, datasets, atlases, protocols, benchmarks.
